arxiv-2111-05963.title: Gravitational lensing of Continuous Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2111-05963.creator: Marek Biesiada, Sreekanth Harikumar
arxiv-2111-05963.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Marek Biesiada, Sreekanth Harikumar. Continuous gravitational waves are analogous to monochromatic light and therefore could be used to detect wave effects like interference or diffraction. This would be possible with strongly lensed gravitational waves. This article reviews and summaries the theory of gravitational lensing in the context of gravitational waves in two different regimes: geometric optics and wave optics, for two widely used lens models such as point mass lens and Singular Isothermal Sphere (SIS).

arxiv-2207-07134.title: New phases of 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM at finite chemical potential
arxiv-2207-07134.creator: Óscar J.C. Dias, Prahar Mitra, and Jorge E. Santos
arxiv-2207-07134.description: Abstract We do a systematic search of supergravity solutions that, via the AdS 5 /CFT 4 correspondence, are dual to thermal states in 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM at finite chemical potential. These solutions dominate the microcanonical ensemble and are required to ultimately reproduce the microscopic entropy of AdS black holes.

arxiv-2308-07529.title: The Redshift Difference in Gravitational Lensed Systems: A Novel Probe of Cosmology 2023 The Redshift Difference in Gravitational Lensed Systems: A Novel Probe of Cosmology – References
arxiv-2308-07529.creator: Chengyi Wang, Krzysztof Bolejko, Geraint F. Lewis
arxiv-2308-07529.description: Abstract The exploration of the redshift drift, a direct measurement of cosmological expansion, is expected to take several decades of observation with stable, sensitive instruments. We introduced a new method to probe cosmology which bypasses the long-period observation by observing the redshift difference , an accumulation of the redshift drift, in multiple-image gravitational lens systems.

arxiv-2502-00304.title: HoP: Homeomorphic Polar Learning for Hard Constrained Optimization
arxiv-2502-00304.creator: Ke Deng, Hanwen Zhang, Jin Lu, Haijian Sun
arxiv-2502-00304.description: Abstract Constrained optimization demands highly efficient solvers which promotes the development of learn-to-optimize (L2O) approaches. As a data-driven method, L2O leverages neural networks to efficiently produce approximate solutions. However, a significant challenge remains in ensuring both optimality and feasibility of neural networks’ output.
